title: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: stop-weighting, logprob fallbacks, and structured response shaping
author: Maya Lin
release_notes: Adds v1 chat param parity for stop-weighting and logprob fallback behavior; improves streaming framing and structured output shaping for function/toolcall interoperability. Backwards-compatible; recommended for users relying on /v1/chat.completions semantics.
description: Context: Customers expect the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions semantics (stop arrays, role-preserving tokenization heuristics, and logprob fallbacks for truncated streams) to behave the same when using Redwood's compatibility layer. We observed two recurring issues in production: 1) ambiguous stop precedence when multiple stop tokens and stop weights are provided (edge cases where streaming fragments cause stray punctuation to trigger a premature stop), and 2) structured output/toolcall shapes drifting when streaming backpressure causes partial JSON fragments, leading downstream parsers to misinterpret tool metadata. This PR unifies parameter handling and adds a robust, streaming-aware logprob fallback path plus a structured-output flattener to keep toolcall metadata stable across chunk boundaries. Summary of changes: - Add `stop_weights` merging logic in the v1 param adapter: when callers supply both `stop` and `stop_weights` we canonicalize into an ordered precedence list; we apply a per-token weighted threshold that reduces false positives on punctuation-heavy workloads. - Implement streaming logprob fallback: when a stream is cut due to network/backpressure but the last token boundary is ambiguous, we compute a best-effort logprob summary across the last N tokens and use it to decide whether to emit a STOP event or continue; this preserves parity with OpenAI behavior where logprobs are considered a secondary signal. - Introduce a Structured Response Shaper in the stream coalescer: rehydrates partial JSON/toolcall fragments across frames, validates required tool metadata (name, args, call_id), and emits a single framed toolcall envelope to the client. The balancer includes a lightweight recovery mode that emits a deterministic placeholder if fragments cannot be reconciled after the configured timeout. - Tests: add unit and integration tests for stop weighting, logprob fallback heuristics, and end-to-end streaming toolcall scenarios (including the on-prem installer runbook). - Docs/SDK: update TS and Python adapters to expose the canonicalized v1 param mapping and add an example showing how to opt into stricter stop semantics. Checklist: - [x] Implement core adapter logic and streaming hook - [x] Add unit tests for weighting and fallback heuristics - [x] Add integration tests with the stream rehydration harness - [x] Update SDK examples and docs - [x] Run load test (perf-canary) and check latency/regression targets Why this change matters: Without parity on stop/logprob semantics, clients using Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer hit surprising truncation or malformed toolcall payloads in production (customer-reported). This PR reduces those failure modes and provides a clear config path for teams that need either conservative or permissive stop behavior. Backwards compatibility notes: default behavior preserves existing integrations; the new `stop_weights` merge is opt-out via adapter config. Migration notes: no immediate action required for customers; advanced users can enable stricter stop thresholds via Redwood Console or the SDK flag `v1_stop_strict=true`. Commits: - Initial v1 param adapter and stop_weights merge (m.1d9e3) - Streaming logprob fallback prototype and unit tests (c.2b7f4) - Structured response shaper and stream rehydration harness (a.9f11c) - SDK examples and docs update (d.3c4b1) - Fix: reduce flakiness in toolcall timeout logic (hotfix) (f.6b2a0) Changed files (high-level): - src/compat/openai_v1/params_adapter.py - src/serving/stream/coalescer.py - src/serving/stream/logprob_fallback.py - src/serving/stream/tests/test_stop_weights.py - src/serving/stream/tests/test_toolcall_rehydrate.py - sdk/python/openai_compat_examples/stop_weighting_example.py - sdk/ts/openai_compat_examples/stop_weights_example.ts - docs/openai/v1_chat.md Testing and CI: CI initially failed on flakiness in the integration harness (see CI logs) due to the stream rehydration timeout default being too short; adjusted to 250ms in the harness and re-ran. All checks green on second run (unit tests, integration, lint, mypy, ts-check, canary perf smoke). Performance: microbenchmarks show a median 1.5% token latency increase in the worst-case path (logprob fallback triggered) but a 4x reduction in malformed toolcall incidents on the internal canary dataset. Security review: no new surface area for credentials; structured response placeholder uses deterministic placeholder values and is logged with PII scrubbers applied. Release notes: included above. Merge: squash and merge to main. Related: ENG-2107 (stop parity work), ENG-1234 (streaming stability initiative).
